import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = set(range(len(feats.ids)))
    correlated = set()
    
    # Get correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    # Identify near-duplicates (|r| >= 0.6)
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                # Keep the one with higher effect size
                mean_diff_i = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1,i]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0,i])
                mean_diff_j = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1,j]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0,j])
                
                if abs(mean_diff_i) > abs(mean_diff_j):
                    correlated.add(j)
                else:
                    correlated.add(i)
    
    keep = set(range(len(feats.ids))) - correlated
    
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i in keep:
        mean_diff = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1,i]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0,i])
        effect_sizes.append((abs(mean_diff), i))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    effect_sizes.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top candidates
    candidates = [feats.ids[i] for _, i in effect_sizes[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # If no strong effect, return empty design
    if not candidates:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Check if any candidate has significant correlation with outcome
    drivers = []
    for fid in candidates:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        mean_diff = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1,col_idx]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0,col_idx])
        
        # Welch's t-test
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        
        # Include if effect size is large enough or t-statistic is significant
        if abs(mean_diff) > 0.5 or abs(t_stat) > 3.0:
            drivers.append(fid)
            
    # Limit to at most 4 drivers
    drivers = drivers[:4]
    
    # If we have drivers, include them in columns
    if drivers:
        # Simple logistic regression to get weights
        lr = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=False, max_iter=1000)
        lr.fit(feats.x[:, [feats.column(d) for d in drivers]], feats.y)
        
        # Create weighted score
        loadings = dict(zip(drivers, lr.coef_[0]))
        
        # Return design
        return Design(
            drivers=tuple(drivers),
            columns=tuple(drivers),
            products=(),
            loadings=loadings
        )
    
    # No mechanism found
    return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
